## 3. Naming Conventions

- **Components:** PascalCase `.tsx` — `RecruitmentManagement.tsx`, `ApplicantManagement.tsx`, `BuilderEntitiesCard.tsx`-style names.
- **BUT:** there are **no per-component files**. Modules are **giant monoliths**:
  - `frontend/src/components/modules/RecruitmentManagement.tsx` — **355 KB / ~7,688 lines**
  - `frontend/src/components/modules/ApplicantManagement.tsx` — **822 KB**
 - `frontend/src/components/modules/CoreHCM.tsx` — 238 KB
- **Only exception:** the `ess/` feature folder is properly decomposed per convention: `ess/index.tsx`, `ess/EssManagement.tsx`, `ess/modals/*Modal.tsx`, `ess/tabs/Ess*Tab.tsx`, `ess/shared/*Badge.tsx`. This is the newer, preferred pattern.
- **UI primitives:** `frontend/src/components/ui/<kebab-case>.tsx` (shadcn convention, e.g. `textarea.tsx`, `dialog.tsx`).
- **Routes:** `frontend/src/routes/admin/_<module>/<page>.tsx` with a `_` prefix for pathless layout segments (e.g. `routes/admin/_recruitmentmanagement/recruitment.tsx`).
- **Backend:** PSR-4 per module — `Modules\RecruitmentManagement\{Models,Http\Controllers,Http\Requests,Http\Resources,Enums,Services}`, snake_case filenames, PascalCase classes, snake_case tables (`job_posts`, `job_post_platforms`).
- **Stray duplicate files:** `*-DESKTOP-*.tsx` / `*-DESKTOP-*.php` are leftover OneDrive/Desktop copies (e.g. `Settings-DESKTOP-T31RHI0.tsx`, `JobPost-DESKTOP-FJ91I5O.php`). These are stale duplicates — ignore them.

### The 9 blocks (per `docs\JOB_POST_EDITOR_ENTITY_ALIGNMENT.md`)
`title` · `info` · `description` · `responsibilities` · `qualifications` · **`skills`** · `instructions` · `about` · `picture`

Publishing requires title, department and **all six text blocks**; missing blocks are auto-added to the canvas and focus jumps to the first empty one.

### 7b. Requirement Templates → seeds the Required Skills block (line 2485–2566)
```tsx
/** Applies a requirement template to the Job Post Builder draft: skills seed
 *  Required Skills, certifications / job roles seed Qualifications (roles as
 *  an "Experience as …" line) and education / experience entities fill the
 *  structured levels the NLP screening scores against. */
const applyRequirementTemplateToDraft = (template: ApiRequirementTemplate) => {
  const mergeLines = (current: string, additions: string[]) => { /* case-insensitive dedupe */ };

  const skills = template.items.filter(i => i.entity_type === "skill").map(i => i.value);
  const qualificationLines = [
    ...template.items.filter(i => i.entity_type === "certification").map(i => i.value),
    ...template.items.filter(i => i.entity_type === "job_role").map(i => `Experience as ${i.value}`),
    ...template.items.filter(i => i.entity_type === "education" && !isEducationLevel(i.value)).map(i => `Education: ${i.value}`),
    ...template.items.filter(i => i.entity_type === "experience" && !isExperienceLevel(i.value)).map(i => `Experience: ${i.value}`),
  ];
  const educationLevel = template.items.filter(i => i.entity_type === "education")
    .map(i => isEducationLevel(i.value)).find(l => l !== undefined);
  const experienceLevel = /* ...same for experience... */;

  const nextSkills = mergeLines(draft.skills, skills);
  const nextQualifications = mergeLines(draft.qualifications, qualificationLines);

  setDraft(d => ({ ...d, skills: nextSkills.join("\n"), qualifications: nextQualifications.join("\n"),
                   ...(educationLevel ? { educationLevel } : {}),
                   ...(experienceLevel ? { experienceLevel } : {}) }));
  setBlocks(b => {                                   // ensure blocks exist on canvas
    const needed = (["skills", "qualifications"] as BlockId[]).filter(id => !b.includes(id));
    return needed.length ? [...b, ...needed] : b;
  });
  setActiveBlock("skills");
  setScreeningOpen(false); setTab("builder"); setBuilderStarted(true); setBuilderTemplatePick("");
  toast.success(`Requirement template "${template.name}" applied to the job post`, { ... });
};
```

## 10. Practical Notes for Modifying the Builder

1. **There is no `JobPostBuilder.tsx` to edit.** Everything lives in `RecruitmentManagement.tsx`. Target line ranges: block JSX `6113–6507`, `Draft` type `1087–1131`, block registry `979–1012`.
2. **`draft.skills` is a newline-delimited `string`**, converted to `string[]` via `lines()` at save time. If you want a tag/chip UI, you must keep the string↔array round-trip at `jobToDraft` (1154) and the payload build (3279).
3. **Adding a field requires 4 edits:** `Draft` type, `blankDraft`, `jobToDraft`, and the block JSX — plus backend migration + `StoreJobPostRequest`/`UpdateJobPostRequest` + `JobPostResource` + `JobPost` model fillable/casts.
4. **Watch for duplicate/stale files:** `*-DESKTOP-*` variants and `backend-laravel\app\Models\JobPost.php` vs `Modules\RecruitmentManagement\app\Models\JobPost.php`. The module one is the live one.
5. The `ess/` folder shows the target decomposition pattern (`index.tsx` + `tabs/` + `modals/` + `shared/`) if the builder ever gets extracted.
6. `AGENTS.md` at `frontend\` warns this is a **Lovable-connected repo** — do not force-push, rebase, amend, or squash pushed commits.

1: # Job Post Editor — Fields & Entity Alignment
2: 
3: Reference for the **Job Post Builder** in Recruitment Management: what each
4: field is, where its value comes from, and which database entity owns it.
5: 
6: - Frontend: `frontend/src/components/modules/RecruitmentManagement.tsx`
7: - Backend: `backend-laravel/Modules/RecruitmentManagement/`
8: - Core HCM source: `backend-laravel/Modules/CoreHCM/`
9: 
10: ---
11: 
12: ## 1. Field ownership at a glance
13: 
14: Every Job Info field resolves to exactly one owning entity. Nothing is typed
15: twice: the builder reads Core HCM and writes only the recruitment-side record.
16: 
17: | Builder field | Reads from | Written to | Auto? |
18: |---|---|---|---|
19: | Title | `positions.title` | derived on save | auto |
20: | Department | `departments.name` | `job_posts.department_id` | selected |
21: | Type | — | `job_posts.employment_type` | manual |
22: | Schedule | — | `job_posts.schedule` | selected |
23: | **Vacancies** | `requisitions.requested_count`, else `positions.headcount − filled_count` | `job_posts.vacancies` | **auto** |
24: | **Salary min** | `salary_grades.min_salary` via position's band | `job_posts.salary_min` | **auto** |
25: | **Salary max** | `salary_grades.max_salary` via position's band | `job_posts.salary_max` | **auto** |
26: | Education level | requirement templates | `job_posts.education_level` | selected |
27: | Experience level | requirement templates | `job_posts.experience_level` | selected |
28: | Description / Responsibilities / Qualifications / Skills / Instructions / About | AI draft or manual | `*_json` columns | manual / AI |
29: | Picture of hiring | upload | `job_posts.picture` | manual |
30: 
31: ---
32: 
33: ## 2. Entity relationship
34: 
35: ```
36: departments ──1:N──> positions ──1:N──> job_posts ──1:N──> applicants
37:       │                    │                 │
38:       │                    │                 └──> job_post_platforms (Website/Facebook/Instagram/Indeed)
39:       │                    │
40:       │                    ├──N:1──> salary_grades   (the band: min_salary / max_salary)
41:       │                    │                 │
42:       │                    │                 └──> source of Salary min / max
43:       │                    │
44:       │                    └── headcount / filled_count  (source of Vacancies)
45:       │
46:       └── name (label shown in the builder)
47: 
48: requisitions ──> departments + positions      (requested_count → Vacancies)
49:       │
50:       └── converted_job_post_id ──> job_posts  (Pending → Done → Converted)
51: ```
52: 
53: ### Ownership rules
54: 
55: | Entity | Owns | Never stores |
56: |---|---|---|
57: | `departments` | name, code, head | vacancy counts |
58: | `positions` | title, headcount, filled_count, salary_grade_id | posting text, published status |
59: | `salary_grades` | code, title, min_salary, max_salary, level | which post uses it |
60: | `requisitions` | requested_count, urgency, justification, status | salary, published content |
61: | `job_posts` | the published ad: salary, vacancies, content, platforms | headcount (lives on the position) |
62: 
63: `positions.headcount − positions.filled_count` is the **open slots** figure.
64: `PositionResource` already exposes it as a computed `vacancies` field, so no
65: extra column is required.
66: 
67: ---
68: 
69: ## 3. Auto-filled fields
70: 
71: ### 3.1 Salary min / max
72: 
73: The band is resolved from Core HCM and written straight into the two inputs.
74: No grade selector, no "apply" button.
75: 
76: ```
77: positions.salary_grade_id ──> salary_grades ──> min_salary / max_salary
78:                                                      │
79:                                                      ▼
80:                                         Salary min (₱) / Salary max (₱)
81: ```
82: 
83: Resolution order for the band:
84: 
85: 1. `draft.salaryGradeId` (set when a position is chosen)
86: 2. `draftPosition.salaryGradeId` — the position's assigned grade
87: 3. `draftPosition.salaryGradeMin/Max` — band values already resolved on load
88: 
89: Behaviour:
90: 
91: - Picking a position or linking a requisition fills both fields automatically.
92: - Typing a figure sets `salaryLocked` — your number is then preserved.
93: - Changing the position/grade re-arms the sync (`bandSourceRef`), refilling both.
94: - **Reset to band** appears under Salary max only while `salaryLocked` is true;
95:   it clears the lock and restores the Core HCM figures.
96: - `Edit Template` starts locked so an already-published post's live salary is
97:   never silently rewritten.
98: 
99: ### 3.2 Vacancies
100: 
101: Priority order:
102: 
103: | # | Source | Value | Label shown to HR |
104: |---|--------|-------|-------------------|
105: | 1 | Linked requisition | `requested_count` | requisition `REQ-00007` |
106: | 2 | Core HCM position | `headcount − filled_count` | open slots |
107: | 3 | Neither | `1` | — |
108: 
109: - Floor of **1**: a fully-staffed position still needs a posting.
110: - Floor of **filled**: a post can never advertise fewer slots than the hires it
111:   already recorded.
112: - Editing the field sets `vacanciesLocked`; **Reset vacancies** restores the
113:   Core HCM figure.
114: - Changing the position or requisition re-arms the sync automatically
115:   (`vacancySourceRef`).
116: - Admins converting from a requisition get the input `disabled` — the requested
117:   count is authoritative and must not be hand-edited.
118: 
119: ---
120: 
121: ## 4. Editor flow
122: 
123: ```
124:                     ┌──────────────────────────────┐
125:   New post ─────────>│                              │
126:   Copy & Use ──────>│      JOB POST BUILDER        │──> Save draft ──> status: Draft
127:   Convert req ─────>│   (9 draggable content       │                  active: false
128:   Edit Template ───>│    blocks + Job Info)        │──> Publish  ───> status: Open
129:                     │                              │                  active: true
130:                     └──────────────────────────────┘
131: ```
132: 
133: ### Entry points and their seeding
134: 
135: | Entry | `editingJobId` | Salary | Vacancies |
136: |---|---|---|---|
137: | **New post** | `null` | auto from band | auto from position |
138: | **Copy & Use Template** | `null` | auto (unlocked) | auto (unlocked) |
139: | **Convert requisition** | `null` | auto from band | requested count, locked for admins |
140: | **Edit Template** | job id | **locked** — keeps published values | **locked** — keeps published values |
141: | **Link pending request** | unchanged | re-armed | re-armed |
142: 
143: ### The 9 blocks
144: 
145: | Block | Content |
146: |---|---|
147: | `title` | Position + department pickers |
148: | `info` | Type, schedule, vacancies, salary min/max, education, experience |
149: | `description` | Job description |
150: | `responsibilities` | Key responsibilities |
151: | `qualifications` | Qualifications |
152: | `skills` | Required skills |
153: | `instructions` | Application instructions |
154: | `about` | About the company |
155: | `picture` | Hiring poster upload |
156: 
157: Publishing requires title, department, and all six text blocks. Missing blocks
158: are added to the canvas automatically and focus moves to the first one.
159: 
160: ---
161: 
162: ## 5. Server-side behaviour
163: 
164: `RecruitmentManagementController`:
165: 
166: | Concern | Behaviour |
167: |---|---|
168: | Salary defaulting | `applyPositionSalaryDefaults()` fills blank `salary_min`/`salary_max` from the position's grade — called in **both** `store()` and `update()` |
169: | Title / slug | Derived from the linked position by the `JobPost` model, so a post can never drift from its position |
170: | Duplicate guard | One posting per position + department; `POST` → 409 `DUPLICATE_JOB_POST` with `existing_job_post_id`; `PUT` only 409s when the pair genuinely changes |
171: | Poster serving | `GET /job-posts/{id}/picture` tries several legacy paths, falls back to the composed template poster, never 404s |
172: | Vacancy lifecycle | `fillOneSlot()` increments `filled_count` and auto-closes the post at 0 slots |
173: | Position creation | `StorePositionRequest` requires `salary_grade_id` and `headcount ≥ 1` |
174: 
175: ---
176: 
177: ## 6. Known gaps
178: 
179: | Gap | Impact |
180: |---|---|
181: | `job_posts.vacancies` is never validated against `positions.headcount` | A post can advertise more slots than HR approved |
182: | `UpdateJobPostRequest` drops the `gte:salary_min` check that `StoreJobPostRequest` has | An edit can save `salary_max < salary_min` |
183: | Salary band can only be changed in Core HCM, not the builder | Recruiters must leave the job post screen to move a role to another band |
184: | A stale duplicate `JobPost` model exists at `backend-laravel/app/Models/JobPost.php` | Missing `requires_practical` / `picture`; the module model is the one controllers use |
185: | The `info` block is ~200 lines of JSX inside an 8,000-line file | Candidate for extraction into a `JobInfoPanel` component |

500: interface BuilderEntityIndex {
501:   exact: Map<string, string>;

505: /** Flattens {canonical: aliases} into an exact lookup plus longest-first keys. */
506: function buildBuilderEntityIndex(mapping: Record<string, string[]>): BuilderEntityIndex {
507:   const exact = new Map<string, string>();
508:   Object.entries(mapping ?? {}).forEach(([canonical, aliases]) => {
509:     const canonKey = normalizeEntityText(canonical);
510:     if (canonKey && !exact.has(canonKey)) exact.set(canonKey, canonical);
511:     (aliases ?? []).forEach((alias) => {
512:       const key = normalizeEntityText(alias);
513:       if (key && !exact.has(key)) exact.set(key, canonical);
514:     });
515:   });
516:   return { exact, keys: [...exact.keys()].sort((a, b) => b.length - a.length) };
517: }
518: 
519: /** Exact → boundary-substring → token-containment, like the NLP service. */
520: function canonicalizeBuilderEntity(value: string, index: BuilderEntityIndex): string | null {
521:   const norm = normalizeEntityText(value);
522:   if (!norm) return null;
523:   const direct = index.exact.get(norm);
524:   if (direct) return direct;
525:   const padded = ` ${norm} `;
526:   for (const key of index.keys) {
527:     if (key.length >= 4 && padded.includes(` ${key} `)) return index.exact.get(key) ?? null;
528:   }
529:   const valueTokens = new Set(norm.split(" "));
530:   let best: string | null = null;
531:   let bestLen = 0;
532:   for (const key of index.keys) {
533:     const keyTokens = key.split(" ");
534:     if (keyTokens.length < 2 || key.length <= bestLen) continue;
535:     if (keyTokens.every((t) => valueTokens.has(t))) {
536:       best = index.exact.get(key) ?? null;
537:       bestLen = key.length;
538:     }
539:   }
540:   return best;
541: }

548: /** Splits filled lines into recognized canonicals vs unrecognized raw lines. */
549: function analyzeBuilderEntityLines(

551:   index: BuilderEntityIndex,
552: ): { recognized: BuilderEntityHit[]; unrecognized: string[] } {
553:   const recognized = new Map<string, string>();
554:   const unrecognized: string[] = [];
555:   const seenUnrecognized = new Set<string>();
556:   rawLines.forEach((raw) => {
557:     const line = raw.trim();
558:     if (!line) return;
559:     const hits = new Set<string>();

567:       }

572:         seenUnrecognized.add(key);

574:       }

576:       hits.forEach((canonical) => {
577:         if (!recognized.has(canonical)) recognized.set(canonical, line);

598:   weights: { skills: 40, experience: 30, education: 20, certifications: 10 },
599:   passingScore: 75,
600:   coverageMin: 0.6,
601:   live: false,
602: };

604: /** Reads live weights out of the saved/effective screening configuration. */
605: function builderScoringFromConfig(
606:   effective: ScreeningConfiguration | null | undefined,
607: ): BuilderScoringRef {
608:   if (!effective) return DEFAULT_BUILDER_SCORING;
609:   const findWeight = (match: string, fallback: number): number => {
610:     const entry = Object.entries(effective.criteria ?? {}).find(([name]) =>
611:       name.toLowerCase().includes(match),
612:     );
613:     const raw = entry ? Number(entry[1]?.weight) : NaN;
614:     if (!Number.isFinite(raw)) return fallback;
615:     // Stored either as percent (40) or fraction (0.4).
616:     return raw > 0 && raw <= 1 ? raw * 100 : raw;
617:   };
618:   const coverageRaw = Number(effective.required_skills_coverage_min);
619:   const passingRaw = Number((effective as { passing_score?: unknown }).passing_score);
620:   return {
621:     weights: {
622:       skills: findWeight("skill", 40),
623:       experience: findWeight("experience", 30),
624:       education: findWeight("education", 20),
625:       certifications: findWeight("cert", 10),
626:     },
627:     passingScore: Number.isFinite(passingRaw) ? passingRaw : 75,
628:     coverageMin: Number.isFinite(coverageRaw) ? coverageRaw : 0.6,
629:     live: true,
630:   };
631: }

245:                 $requirements,

291:     /**
292:      * Preview screening WITH staged supporting documents (Add Applicant wizard
293:      * Step 3). The applicant does not exist yet, so documents cannot be stored
294:      * or verified through DocumentVerificationService — instead each staged
295:      * file is verified in-memory against the freshly screened resume profile,
296:      * then the ranking is reclassified with that evidence so Step 3 shows the
297:      * same blended percentage + Resume vs Documents breakdown as the saved
298:      * applicant view.
299:      *
300:      * $documents: list of ['stored_path' => local-disk tmp path,
301:      *   'original_name' => string, 'doc_type' => string, 'title' => ?string]
302:      */
303:     public function screenPreviewWithDocuments(
304:         string $storedPath,
305:         string $originalName,
306:         int $jobPostId,
307:         array $documents = []
308:     ): array {
309:         $jobPost = JobPost::find($jobPostId);
310:         if (! $jobPost) {
311:             return ['success' => false, 'processing_status' => 'FAILED', 'error' => "Job post {$jobPostId} not found."];
312:         }
313: 
314:         $absolutePath = Storage::disk('local')->path($storedPath);
315:         $response = $this->nlp->screenResumeStructured(
316:             $absolutePath,
317:             $originalName,
318:             $this->buildRequirements($jobPost),
319:             $this->buildOpenJobs($jobPost),
320:             referenceData: $this->referenceData(),
321:             screeningSettings: self::screeningSettings()
322:         );
323: 
324:         if (! $response['ok']) {
325:             return ['success' => false, 'processing_status' => 'FAILED', 'error' => $response['error']];
326:         }
327: 
328:         $result = $response['data'] ?? null;
329:         if (! is_array($result) || ! ($result['success'] ?? false)) {
330:             return is_array($result) ? $result : ['success' => false, 'processing_status' => 'FAILED', 'error' => 'Unexpected NLP response.'];
331:         }
332: 
333:         if ($documents === []) {
334:             return $result;
335:         }
336: 
337:         $profile = $result['profile'] ?? null;
338:         if (! is_array($profile) || $profile === []) {
339:             $result['preview_documents'] = [];
340: 
341:             return $result;
342:         }
343: 
344:         $referenceData = $this->referenceData();
345:         $previewDocs = [];
346:         $docVerifications = [];
347: 
348:         foreach (array_values($documents) as $i => $doc) {
349:             $docPath = (string) ($doc['stored_path'] ?? '');
350:             $docOriginal = (string) ($doc['original_name'] ?? 'document');
351:             $docType = (string) ($doc['doc_type'] ?? 'Others');
352:             $title = isset($doc['title']) && $doc['title'] !== '' ? (string) $doc['title'] : $docOriginal;
353:             $previewId = -($i + 1);
354: 
355:             $checks = [];
356:             $summary = null;
357:             $extracted = null;
358:             $status = 'UNABLE_TO_VERIFY';
359: 
360:             try {
361:                 $absoluteDoc = $docPath !== '' ? Storage::disk('local')->path($docPath) : null;
362:                 if ($absoluteDoc && is_file($absoluteDoc)) {
363:                     $verify = $this->nlp->verifySupportingDocument(
364:                         $absoluteDoc,
365:                         $docOriginal,
366:                         $docType,
367:                         $profile,
368:                         $referenceData
369:                     );
370:                     $data = $verify['data'] ?? null;
371:                     if (is_array($data)) {
372:                         $status = (string) ($data['verification_status'] ?? 'UNABLE_TO_VERIFY');
373:                         $checks = is_array($data['checks'] ?? null) ? $data['checks'] : [];
374:                         $summary = $data['summary'] ?? ($verify['error'] ?? null);
375:                         $extracted = $data['extracted_document_profile'] ?? null;
376:                     } else {
377:                         $summary = $verify['error'] ?? 'Document verification failed.';
378:                     }
379:                 } else {
380:                     $summary = 'The staged document file could not be read, so no comparison was possible.';
381:                 }
382:             } catch (\Throwable $e) {
383:                 Log::warning('Preview document verification failed: ' . $e->getMessage());
384:                 $summary = 'Automatic verification failed: ' . $e->getMessage();
385:             }
386: 
387:             $previewDocs[] = [
388:                 'applicant_document_id' => $previewId,
389:                 'applicant_id' => 0,
390:                 'doc_type' => $docType,
391:                 'title' => $title,
392:                 'original_copy' => false,
393:                 'file_path' => null,
394:                 'original_name' => $docOriginal,
395:                 'uploaded_at' => null,
396:                 'verification_status' => $status,
397:                 'verification_result' => [
398:                     'success' => $status === 'VERIFIED',
399:                     'document_type' => $docType,
400:                     'verification_status' => $status,
401:                     'checks' => $checks,
402:                     'summary' => $summary,
403:                 ],
404:                 'extracted_profile' => $extracted,
405:                 'verified_at' => null,
406:             ];
407:             $docVerifications[] = [
408:                 'applicant_document_id' => $previewId,
409:                 'doc_type' => $docType,
410:                 'verification_status' => $status,
411:                 'verification_result' => [
412:                     'checks' => $checks,
413:                     'summary' => $summary,
414:                 ],

416:         }

418:         // Blend the staged evidence into the ranking so the percentage shown

422:                 'profile' => $profile,
423:                 'validation' => is_array($result['validation'] ?? null) ? $result['validation'] : [],
424:                 'requirements' => $this->buildRequirements($jobPost),
425:                 'open_jobs' => $this->buildOpenJobs($jobPost),
426:                 'document_verifications' => $docVerifications,
427:                 'screening_settings' => self::screeningSettings(),
428:                 'reference_data' => $referenceData,
429:             ]);
430:             $blended = ($re['ok'] ?? false) ? ($re['data'] ?? null) : null;
431:             if (is_array($blended) && ($blended['success'] ?? false)) {
432:                 $result['resume_match_score'] = $result['match_score'] ?? ($result['resume_match_score'] ?? null);
433:                 $result['match_score'] = $blended['match_score'] ?? $result['match_score'];
434:                 $result['screening_status'] = $blended['screening_status'] ?? ($result['screening_status'] ?? null);
435:                 $result['document_verification'] = $blended['document_verification'] ?? ($result['document_verification'] ?? null);
436:                 if (array_key_exists('alternative_job', $blended)) {
437:                     $result['alternative_job'] = $blended['alternative_job'];
438:                 }
439:                 if (array_key_exists('screening_reasons', $blended)) {
440:                     $result['screening_reasons'] = $blended['screening_reasons'];
441:                 }
442:             }
443:         } catch (\Throwable $e) {
444:             Log::warning('Preview ranking reclassify failed: ' . $e->getMessage());
445:         }

447:         $result['preview_documents'] = $previewDocs;
448: 
449:         return $result;

452:     /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
453:     /* Supporting-document evidence                                        */
454:     /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
455: 
456:     /**
457:      * The applicant's supporting documents expressed for the NLP classifier.
458:      * Every stored verification result is forwarded (PENDING/verifying rows
459:      * included — the NLP side ignores those), so the evidence block in the
460:      * screening result always mirrors the applicant's real document set.
461:      */
462:     public function documentVerifications(Applicant $applicant): array
463:     {
464:         return $applicant->documents()
465:             ->whereNotNull('verification_status')
466:             ->orderBy('applicant_document_id')
467:             ->get()
468:             ->map(function ($document) {
469:                 $result = is_array($document->verification_result_json)
470:                     ? $document->verification_result_json
471:                     : [];
472: 
473:                 return [
474:                     'applicant_document_id' => (int) $document->applicant_document_id,
475:                     'doc_type' => $document->doc_type,
476:                     'verification_status' => $document->verification_status,
477:                     'verification_result' => [
478:                         'checks' => $result['checks'] ?? [],
479:                         'summary' => $result['summary'] ?? null,
480:                     ],
481:                 ];
482:             })
483:             ->all();
484:     }
485: 
486:     /**
487:      * Human-readable explanation of the document evidence for the applicant
488:      * summary line; null when no decisive document participated in the score
489:      * (no documents, still verifying, or nothing comparable).
490:      */
491:     protected function documentEvidenceSentence(array $result): ?string
492:     {
493:         $evidence = $result['document_verification'] ?? null;
494:         if (! is_array($evidence)
495:             || ! in_array($evidence['status'] ?? '', ['VERIFIED', 'PARTIAL', 'DISCREPANCY'], true)) {
496:             return null;
497:         }
498: 
499:         $score = function ($value): string {
500:             if (! is_numeric($value)) {
501:                 return '—';
502:             }
503: 
504:             return rtrim(rtrim(number_format((float) $value, 2, '.', ''), '0'), '.');
505:         };
506: 
507:         return sprintf(
508:             'Supporting-document verification: %d verified, %d with discrepancies, %d unable to verify — ranking score %s%% (resume match %s%%).',
509:             (int) ($evidence['verified_count'] ?? 0),
510:             (int) ($evidence['discrepancy_count'] ?? 0),
511:             (int) ($evidence['unable_count'] ?? 0),
512:             $score($result['match_score'] ?? null),
513:             $score($result['resume_match_score'] ?? null)
514:         );
515:     }
516: 
517:     /**
518:      * Evidence flags for the applicant's flags_json, prefixed so they can be
519:      * refreshed on recompute without disturbing the resume-screening flags.
520:      */
521:     protected function documentEvidenceFlags(array $result): array
522:     {
523:         $flags = [];
524:         foreach (($result['document_verification']['flags'] ?? []) as $flag) {
525:             if (is_string($flag) && $flag !== '') {
526:                 $flags[] = '[DOCUMENT] ' . $flag;
527:             }
528:         }
529: 
530:         return $flags;
531:     }
532: 
533:     /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
534:     /* Persistence                                                         */
535:     /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
536: 
537:     public function persistResult(Applicant $applicant, JobPost $jobPost, ?array $result, ?string $error = null): ?ApplicantScreening
538:     {
539:         if (! $result || ! ($result['success'] ?? false)) {
540:             return ApplicantScreening::create([
541:                 'applicant_id' => $applicant->applicant_id,
542:                 'job_post_id' => $jobPost->job_post_id,
543:                 'processing_status' => 'FAILED',
544:                 'error_message' => mb_substr($error ?? 'Unknown screening failure', 0, 1000),
545:                 'processed_at' => now(),
546:             ]);
547:         }
548: 
549:         $official = $result['screening_status'] ?? null;
550:         $statusValue = self::STATUS_MAP[$official] ?? null;
551: 
552:         $screening = ApplicantScreening::create([
553:             'applicant_id' => $applicant->applicant_id,
554:             'job_post_id' => $jobPost->job_post_id,
555:             'processing_status' => $result['processing_status'] ?? 'PROCESSED',
556:             'screening_result' => $statusValue,
557:             'match_score' => $result['match_score'] ?? null,
558:             /* Resume-only score before the supporting-document evidence was
559:                blended in (Candidate Ranking shows the blended match_score). */
560:             'resume_match_score' => $result['resume_match_score'] ?? null,
561:             'score_breakdown_json' => $result['score_breakdown'] ?? null,
562:             'profile_json' => $result['profile'] ?? null,
563:             'entities_json' => $result['entities'] ?? null,
564:             'missing_information_json' => $result['validation']['missing_information'] ?? [],
565:             'validation_json' => $result['validation'] ?? null,
566:             'alternative_job_json' => $result['alternative_job'] ?? null,
567:             'document_verification_json' => $result['document_verification'] ?? null,
568:             'reasons_json' => $result['screening_reasons'] ?? [],
569:             'model_info_json' => $result['model_info'] ?? null,
570:             'error_message' => $error,
571:             'processed_at' => now(),
572:         ]);
573: 
574:         // Refresh entity + score breakdown rows (existing tables, reused).
575:         $applicant->screeningEntities()->delete();
576:         foreach (($result['entities'] ?? []) as $entity) {
577:             ApplicantScreeningEntity::create([
578:                 'applicant_id' => $applicant->applicant_id,
579:                 'label' => mb_substr((string) ($entity['label'] ?? ''), 0, 80),
580:                 'value' => (string) ($entity['value'] ?? ''),
581:             ]);
582:         }
583: 
584:         $applicant->screeningScores()->delete();
585:         foreach (($result['score_breakdown'] ?? []) as $criterion => $component) {
586:             ApplicantScreeningScore::create([
587:                 'applicant_id' => $applicant->applicant_id,
588:                 'criterion' => ucfirst($criterion),
589:                 'score' => (float) ($component['earned'] ?? 0),
590:             ]);
591:         }
592: 
593:         // Update the applicant row itself (fit_score, status, summary, flags).
594:         $flags = [];
595: 
596:         $validation = $result['validation'] ?? [];
597:         foreach (($validation['invalid_format'] ?? []) as $invalid) {
598:             $flags[] = $invalid;
599:         }
600:         foreach (($validation['skill_analysis']['unrecognized'] ?? []) as $skill) {
601:             $flags[] = "Unrecognized skill: {$skill}";
602:         }
603:         foreach (($validation['job_role_analysis']['unrecognized'] ?? []) as $role) {
604:             $flags[] = "Unrecognized job role: {$role}";
605:         }
606:         foreach (($validation['missing_information'] ?? []) as $missing) {
607:             $flags[] = "Missing: {$missing}";
608:         }
609:         foreach (($validation['credential_verification']['flags'] ?? []) as $vFlag) {
610:             $severity = $vFlag['severity'] ?? 'WARNING';
611:             $detail = $vFlag['detail'] ?? '';
612:             if ($detail !== '') {
613:                 $flags[] = "[{$severity}] {$detail}";
614:             }
615:         }
616: 
617:         /* Supporting-document evidence (verified / discrepancy / unable) — the
618:            same sentences shown next to the ranking percentage in the UI. */
619:         foreach ($this->documentEvidenceFlags($result) as $documentFlag) {
620:             $flags[] = $documentFlag;
621:         }
622: 
623:         $alternative = $result['alternative_job'] ?? null;
624:         if ($alternative) {
625:             $flags[] = sprintf(
626:                 'Stronger match: %s (%s%%)',
627:                 $alternative['title'] ?? 'Other position',
628:                 rtrim(rtrim((string) ($alternative['alternative_match_score'] ?? ''), '0'), '.')
629:             );
630:         }
631: 
632:         $summaryParts = [$result['matched_summary'] ?? null];
633: 
634:         /* Explain how the supporting documents moved the ranking score, so the
635:            single percentage shown in Candidate Ranking is self-explanatory. */
636:         $evidenceSentence = $this->documentEvidenceSentence($result);
637:         if ($evidenceSentence) {
638:             $summaryParts[] = $evidenceSentence;
639:         }
640: 
641:         if ($statusValue === 'credential') {
642:             $verificationSummary = $validation['credential_verification']['summary'] ?? null;
643:             if ($verificationSummary) {
644:                 $summaryParts[] = $verificationSummary;
645:             } else {
646:                 $summaryParts[] = 'Invalid credential or requires verification based on system validation rules.';
647:             }
648:         } elseif ($statusValue === 'not-fit') {
649:             $summaryParts[] = 'No available position achieved the required qualification level.';
650:         }
651: 
652:         $summary = trim(implode(' ', array_filter($summaryParts)));
653:         if ($summary === '') {
654:             $summary = "Automated spaCy screening completed for {$jobPost->title}.";
655:         }
656: 
657:         $applicant->update([
658:             'fit_score' => $result['match_score'] ?? $applicant->fit_score,
659:             'status' => $statusValue ?? $applicant->status,
660:             'summary' => $summary,
661:             'flags_json' => $flags,
662:         ]);
663: 
664:         return $screening;
665:     }

667:     /**
668:      * Recomputes the applicant's latest screening result with the CURRENT
669:      * supporting-document evidence. Called after a document is uploaded,
670:      * re-verified or deleted, so the candidate's ranking percentage, rank
671:      * order and official status reflect the verification of the resume claims
672:      * without re-uploading or re-OCR-ing the resume: the stored profile +
673:      * validation are replayed through the NLP classification stage.
674:      *
675:      * Returns the updated ApplicantScreening, or null when there is nothing to
676:      * recompute (no screening yet, job post gone, or NLP unavailable).
677:      */
678:     public function recomputeWithDocuments(Applicant $applicant): ?ApplicantScreening
679:     {
680:         $screening = $applicant->screenings()->latest('screening_id')->first();
681:         $profile = $screening?->profile_json;
682: 
683:         if (! $screening || ! is_array($profile) || $profile === []) {
684:             // Documents uploaded before the resume was ever screened stay
685:             // PENDING; the next screening run picks them up automatically.
686:             return null;
687:         }
688: 
689:         $jobPost = JobPost::find($screening->job_post_id ?? $applicant->job_post_id);
690:         if (! $jobPost) {
691:             return null;
692:         }
693: 
694:         $response = $this->nlp->reclassifyScreening([
695:             'profile' => $profile,
696:             'validation' => is_array($screening->validation_json) ? $screening->validation_json : [],
697:             'requirements' => $this->buildRequirements($jobPost),
698:             'open_jobs' => $this->buildOpenJobs($jobPost),
699:             'document_verifications' => $this->documentVerifications($applicant),
700:             'screening_settings' => self::screeningSettings(),
701:             'reference_data' => $this->referenceData(),
702:         ]);
703: 
704:         $data = $response['ok'] ? ($response['data'] ?? null) : null;
705: 
706:         if (! is_array($data) || ! ($data['success'] ?? false)) {
707:             Log::warning(sprintf(
708:                 'Supporting-document recompute failed for applicant %d: %s',
709:                 $applicant->applicant_id,
710:                 $response['error'] ?? 'unexpected NLP response'
711:             ));
712: 
713:             return null;
714:         }
715: 
716:         $statusValue = self::STATUS_MAP[$data['screening_status'] ?? ''] ?? null;
717: 
718:         $screening->update([
719:             'screening_result' => $statusValue ?? $screening->screening_result,
720:             'match_score' => $data['match_score'] ?? $screening->match_score,
721:             'resume_match_score' => $data['resume_match_score'] ?? $screening->resume_match_score,
722:             'document_verification_json' => $data['document_verification'] ?? $screening->document_verification_json,
723:             'alternative_job_json' => $data['alternative_job'] ?? null,
724:             'reasons_json' => $data['screening_reasons'] ?? $screening->reasons_json,
725:             'processed_at' => now(),
726:         ]);
727: 
728:         /* Keep the applicant's ranking fields in sync: Candidate Ranking, the
729:            Top 5 list and the applicants table all read fit_score + status. */
730:         $flags = array_values(array_filter(
731:             $applicant->flags_json ?? [],
732:             fn ($flag) => ! is_string($flag) || ! str_starts_with($flag, '[DOCUMENT]')
733:         ));
734:         foreach ($this->documentEvidenceFlags($data) as $documentFlag) {
735:             $flags[] = $documentFlag;
736:         }
737: 
738:         $summaryParts = array_filter([$data['matched_summary'] ?? null]);
739:         $evidenceSentence = $this->documentEvidenceSentence($data);
740:         if ($evidenceSentence) {
741:             $summaryParts[] = $evidenceSentence;
742:         }
743:         $summary = trim(implode(' ', $summaryParts)) ?: $applicant->summary;
744: 
745:         $applicant->update([
746:             'fit_score' => $data['match_score'] ?? $applicant->fit_score,
747:             'status' => $statusValue ?? $applicant->status,
748:             'summary' => $summary,
749:             'flags_json' => $flags,
750:         ]);
751: 
752:         return $screening->refresh();
753:     }
754: }

38:         if ($request->filled('position_id')) {
39:             $query->where('position_id', (int) $request->input('position_id'));
40:         }
41:         if ($request->has('active')) {
42:             $query->where('active', $request->boolean('active'));
43:         }
44: 
45:         $rows = $query->get()
46:             ->map(fn (ScreeningRequirementTemplate $template) => $this->toPayload($template))
47:             ->values()
48:             ->all();
49: 
50:         return response()->json(['success' => true, 'data' => $rows]);
51:     }
52: 
53:     /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
54:     /* POST /api/v1/screening/requirement-templates                        */
55:     /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
56: 
57:     public function store(Request $request): JsonResponse
58:     {
59:         $data = $this->validated($request);
60: 
61:         $template = DB::transaction(function () use ($data) {
62:             $template = ScreeningRequirementTemplate::create([
63:                 'name' => trim($data['name']),
64:                 'position_id' => $data['position_id'],
65:                 'description' => $data['description'] ?? null,
66:                 'active' => $data['active'] ?? true,
67:             ]);
68: 
69:             $template->items()->createMany($data['items']);
70: 
71:             return $template;
72:         });
73: 
74:         $template->load(['items', 'position']);
75: 
76:         AuditLogger::log(
77:             action: 'Requirement Template Created',
78:             module: 'Applicant Management',
79:             severity: 'Info',
80:             targetType: 'Screening Requirement Template',
81:             targetId: (string) $template->template_id,
82:             details: "Created requirement template '{$template->name}' with "
83:                 . count($data['items']) . ' requirement entities for '
84:                 . ($template->position?->title ?? 'any position') . '.'
85:         );
86: 
87:         return response()->json([
88:             'success' => true,
89:             'data' => $this->toPayload($template),
90:             'message' => 'Requirement template created.',
91:         ], 201);
92:     }
93: 
94:     /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
95:     /* PUT /api/v1/screening/requirement-templates/{id}                    */
96:     /* Replaces the template and all of its requirement entities.          */
97:     /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
98: 
99:     public function update(Request $request, int $id): JsonResponse
100:     {
101:         $template = ScreeningRequirementTemplate::findOrFail($id);
102:         $data = $this->validated($request, $template->template_id);
103: 
104:         DB::transaction(function () use ($template, $data) {
105:             $template->update([
106:                 'name' => trim($data['name']),
107:                 'position_id' => $data['position_id'],
108:                 'description' => $data['description'] ?? null,
109:                 'active' => array_key_exists('active', $data) ? (bool) $data['active'] : $template->active,
110:             ]);
111: 
112:             $template->items()->delete();
113:             $template->items()->createMany($data['items']);
114:         });
115: 
116:         $template->load(['items', 'position']);
117: 
118:         AuditLogger::log(
119:             action: 'Requirement Template Updated',
120:             module: 'Applicant Management',
121:             severity: 'Info',
122:             targetType: 'Screening Requirement Template',
123:             targetId: (string) $template->template_id,
124:             details: "Updated requirement template '{$template->name}' "
125:                 . "({$template->items->count()} requirement entities)."
126:         );
127: 
128:         return response()->json([
129:             'success' => true,
130:             'data' => $this->toPayload($template),
131:             'message' => 'Requirement template updated.',
132:         ]);
133:     }
134: 
135:     /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
136:     /* PATCH /api/v1/screening/requirement-templates/{id}/toggle           */
137:     /* Inactive templates stay stored but are not offered in the builder.  */
138:     /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
139: 
140:     public function toggle(int $id): JsonResponse
141:     {
142:         $template = ScreeningRequirementTemplate::findOrFail($id);
143: 
144:         $template->update(['active' => ! $template->active]);
145:         $template->load(['items', 'position']);
146: 
147:         AuditLogger::log(
148:             action: $template->active ? 'Requirement Template Activated' : 'Requirement Template Deactivated',
149:             module: 'Applicant Management',
150:             severity: 'Info',
151:             targetType: 'Screening Requirement Template',
152:             targetId: (string) $template->template_id,
153:             details: ($template->active ? 'Activated' : 'Deactivated')
154:                 . " requirement template '{$template->name}'."
155:         );
156: 
157:         return response()->json(['success' => true, 'data' => $this->toPayload($template)]);
158:     }
159: 
160:     /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
161:     /* DELETE /api/v1/screening/requirement-templates/{id}                 */
162:     /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
163: 
164:     public function destroy(int $id): JsonResponse
165:     {
166:         $template = ScreeningRequirementTemplate::findOrFail($id);
167:         $details = "{$template->name} (#{$template->template_id})";
168: 
169:         $template->delete();
170: 
171:         AuditLogger::log(
172:             action: 'Requirement Template Deleted',
173:             module: 'Applicant Management',
174:             severity: 'Warning',
175:             targetType: 'Screening Requirement Template',
176:             targetId: (string) $id,
177:             details: "Deleted requirement template '{$details}'."
178:         );
179: 
180:         return response()->json([
181:             'success' => true,
182:             'message' => "Deleted requirement template '{$details}'.",
183:         ]);
184:     }
185: 
186:     /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
187:     /* Helpers                                                             */
188:     /* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
189: 
190:     /**
191:      * Validates the template header + requirement entities. Entities are
192:      * trimmed and de-duplicated per (entity_type, value) so a template can
193:      * never store the same requirement twice.
194:      *
195:      * @return array<string, mixed>
196:      */
197:     private function validated(Request $request, ?int $ignoreId = null): array
198:     {
199:         $rawPosition = $request->input('position_id');
200:         $positionId = ($rawPosition === null || $rawPosition === '' || $rawPosition === 'none')
201:             ? null
202:             : (int) $rawPosition;
203: 
204:         $data = $request->validate([
205:             'name' => [
206:                 'required',
207:                 'string',
208:                 'max:150',
209:                 Rule::unique('screening_requirement_templates', 'name')
210:                     ->where(fn ($query) => $positionId === null
211:                         ? $query->whereNull('position_id')
212:                         : $query->where('position_id', $positionId))
213:                     ->ignore($ignoreId, 'template_id'),
214:             ],
215:             'position_id' => ['nullable', 'integer', 'exists:positions,position_id'],
216:             'description' => ['nullable', 'string', 'max:500'],
217:             'active' => ['boolean'],
218:             'items' => ['required', 'array', 'min:1'],
219:             'items.*.entity_type' => ['required', 'string', Rule::in(ScreeningRequirementTemplateItem::TYPES)],
220:             'items.*.value' => ['required', 'string', 'max:255'],
221:             'items.*.required' => ['boolean'],
222:         ]);
223: 
224:         $items = [];
225:         $seen = [];
226:         foreach ($data['items'] as $item) {
227:             $value = trim((string) ($item['value'] ?? ''));
228:             if ($value === '') {
229:                 continue;
230:             }
231:             $key = $item['entity_type'] . '|' . strtolower($value);
232:             if (isset($seen[$key])) {
233:                 continue;
234:             }
235:             $seen[$key] = true;
236: 
237:             $items[] = [
238:                 'entity_type' => $item['entity_type'],
239:                 'value' => $value,
240:                 'required' => array_key_exists('required', $item) ? (bool) $item['required'] : true,
241:             ];
242:         }
243: 
244:         if ($items === []) {
245:             throw ValidationException::withMessages([
246:                 'items' => 'Add at least one requirement entity to the template.',
247:             ]);
248:         }
249: 
250:         $data['position_id'] = $positionId;
251:         $data['items'] = $items;
252: 
253:         return $data;
254:     }
255: 
256:     /** API shape consumed by the Screening Setup manager and builder picker. */
257:     private function toPayload(ScreeningRequirementTemplate $template): array
258:     {
259:         return [
260:             'template_id' => $template->template_id,
261:             'name' => $template->name,
262:             'position_id' => $template->position_id,
263:             'position_title' => $template->position?->title,
264:             'description' => $template->description,
265:             'active' => (bool) $template->active,
266:             'items' => $template->items
267:                 ->map(fn (ScreeningRequirementTemplateItem $item) => [
268:                     'item_id' => $item->item_id,
269:                     'entity_type' => $item->entity_type,
270:                     'value' => $item->value,
271:                     'required' => (bool) $item->required,
272:                 ])
273:                 ->values()
274:                 ->all(),
275:             'created_at' => $template->created_at?->toISOString(),
276:             'updated_at' => $template->updated_at?->toISOString(),
277:         ];
278:     }
279: }

Key insight to communicate: **`job_posts.skills_json` is the single source of `required_skills`** for the entire NLP screening pipeline. Removing the "Required Skills" block without replacing where the user types skills will silently zero out the skills criterion (40 pts default), break the coverage gate (60%), and make the post get filtered out of `buildOpenJobs()`.

So the answer to "I want to remove the required skills, where should I replace the input" — there are a few options. Let me lay out the design.

The user's three asks:
1. Remove the "Required Skills" block from the job post builder (it always ends up being responsibilities/qualifications duplication).
2. Where should the input be replaced / moved to?
3. How to auto-fill the job post based on the job position → connecting to entity requirements.

Let me think about the right design.

**The duplication problem**: Users type skills like "Communication Skills", "Customer Service", "Time Management" into Required Skills, but they already type "Bachelor's degree", "TESDA NC II" into Qualifications, and duties into Responsibilities. So Required Skills is a third place. And the entity card only reads `draft.skills` for the Skills group.

**Where to replace the input** — options:

**Option A: Merge skills into the Qualifications block** — one textarea, but skills get parsed out. Bad: NLP canonicalization needs clean skill terms, and mixing sentences pollutes matching.

**Option B: Replace the free-text "Required Skills" textarea with a structured "Screening Requirements" panel that is driven by requirement templates / vocabulary** (entity-picker chips). This is the strongest answer, and it directly serves ask #3.

**Option C: Keep Required Skills but make it auto-populated + read-only-ish "derived" view.**

I think the best plan is: **Remove the Required Skills text block from the canvas, and replace it with a "Screening Requirements" section that is derived from the selected position's requirement template.** The user picks a position → template auto-loads → skills become chips → saving writes to `skills_json` (unchanged backend/NLP contract).

This means:
- The user never types skills freehand — they pick from the requirement template (which is HR-managed once per position, reusable across all postings).
- `skills_json` still gets populated → screening unaffected.
- Solves the "always responsibility and qualification" complaint: the skills block no longer competes with the other text blocks.

Let me now think about the concrete implementation.

**1. New `PositionRequirementsPanel` (replaces the `skills` block)**
- Reads `draft.title` → resolves position → finds the matching requirement template (`position_id` match).
- Renders chips grouped by entity type (skill / certification / job_role / education / experience).
- Each chip is a vocabulary-backed term (recognized ✓). Free-text add via combobox with autocomplete from `screeningApi.referenceData.list` skills.
- Editable: add/remove skills, add certs.
- Writes back to `draft.skills` (newline-delimited) so all downstream code is unchanged.

**2. Auto-apply on position selection**

**3. Keep the publish validation**
- Currently publishing requires all six text blocks. Removing `skills` from `fullBlocks` means one less required block. But we should instead validate that the *screening requirements* are non-empty when screening is required.

## How job post relates to the entity for screening

The chain is:

```
Job Post Builder (draft.skills, qualifications, educationLevel, experienceLevel)
   ↓ saved to job_posts.skills_json / qualifications_json / education_level / experience_level
ScreeningService::buildRequirements(JobPost)
   ↓
{ required_skills, preferred_skills: [], education_level, experience_level, required_certifications, required_information }
   ↓ NLP POST
nlp-service match_profile_to_requirements()  (matching.py:149)
   ↓ canonicalize each required skill against reference_data vocabulary
   ↓ skills criterion = 40 pts (live from Screening Setup)
   ↓ required_skills_coverage gate = 60% (fails screening if below)
screening.py:190 → screening_status PERFECT_FOR_THE_JOB / NOT_FITTED_TO_JOB ...
   ↓ persisted
ApplicantScreening + applicants.status/fit_score
```

So: **the ONLY thing that produces `required_skills` is `job_posts.skills_json`**, which is written from `draft.skills`, which is exactly the "Required Skills" textarea.

Therefore: if the Required Skills block is removed, the skills criterion (40/100) silently becomes 0 for every applicant and every post drops out of `buildOpenJobs()` if it has no other criteria.

## Now the design

The user's complaint: "it seems required skills component are not properly included in a job post and it always responsibility and qualification" — I read this as: when they write a job post, they end up putting skills content into Responsibilities/Qualifications because the Required Skills box is awkward (plain newline textarea, no autocomplete, no vocabulary feedback until they flip the card). So the skills block ends up empty or duplicated.

The fix, and answer to "where should I replace the input":

**Replace the free-text "Required Skills" textarea with a structured, position-derived "Screening Requirements" panel.**

Concretely three changes:

### Change 1 — Replace the `skills` block with a `requirements` block (new `PositionRequirementsPanel`)
Instead of a blank textarea, the block:
- resolves the selected position → its `position_id`
- finds the matching active requirement template
- renders skills as **chips** (vocabulary-backed, recognized ✓ / unrecognized +)
- lets HR add/remove skills via a combobox that autocompletes from `screeningApi.referenceData.list`
- writes to `draft.skills` (still newline-delimited string) so **backend + NLP + JobPostResource + `buildRequirements` are all untouched**

This is the key: the storage contract doesn't change, only the input.

### Change 2 — Auto-apply the position's requirement template when a position is picked
`applyPositionToDraft` currently only syncs salary. Extend it:
- resolve `position.dbId`
- find `requirementTemplates.find(t => t.active && t.position_id === position.dbId)`
- if found and the draft's skills are empty (new post) → auto-apply
- if found and skills already exist → ask (or just show a "Apply template" button, not overwrite)

This makes "pick position → requirements are already there", which is exactly the user's ask #3.

### Change 3 — Move the requirement template authoring into the flow + make it the single source of truth
Templates are created once per position in Screening Setup. Optionally: "Create template from this job post" so existing posts can be back-filled.

- Actually: keep `skills` out of the *manual* required set but require **either** template-derived skills **or** AI/typed skills.

The only feedback is on the *back* face (Entities Indicated, `BuilderEntitiesCard`), which most people never flip.

# Option 1: Structured Screening Requirements block

## What replaces the textarea

The `skills` block stops being a blank textarea and becomes a vocabulary-aware panel. The block id stays `"skills"` internally (so every existing code path keeps working) but it is relabelled and re-rendered.

```
╔═ Screening Requirements ═══════════ Auto from "Front Desk Officer" ═╗
║                                                                     ║
║  Skills                                         40 pts · ≈5.7 each   ║
║  (✓) Customer Service        (✕)                (✕) Reservations   ║
║  (✓) Front Office Ops (✕)                (✕) Guest Relations║
║  (◌) MS Office           [ + add to vocabulary ] [ + Add skill ]   ║
║                                                                     ║
║  Certifications                                  10 pts · ≈5 each   ║
║  (✓) TESDA NC II Cookery    (✕)                 [ + Add cert  ]   ║
║                                                                     ║
║  Education level   [ Bachelor's Degree       ▾ ] 20 pts · auto      ║
║  Experience level  [ 1-2 Years               ▾ ] 30 pts · auto      ║
║                                                                     ║
║  From template "Front Office Officer Requirements" · 3 skills, 1 cert║
╚═════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
```

- **(✓)** = the model will recognise it in resumes → green chip
- **(◌)** = not in the screening vocabulary → grey chip + `+` to add it to reference data (inline, not on the hidden back face)
- **(✕)** = remove from this post
- **`+ Add skill`** = a combobox that autocompletes from `screeningApi.referenceData.list`, so HR *physically cannot* type a skill the screener won't match

## Why this fixes your "not properly included" problem

The block reuses `analyzeBuilderEntityLines` (line 549) and `canonicalizeBuilderEntity` (line 520) — **the exact functions that already exist** and already mirror `nlp-service/app/services/reference_data.py:88`. So recognition state shown in the builder is the same answer the screener will give. Today that feedback only exists on the back face at line 839, which is why nobody sees it.

## The concrete edits (all in `RecruitmentManagement.tsx`)

| # | Change | Lines |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Relabel block: `Required Skills` → `Screening Requirements` | 996 |
| 2 | Drop `"skills"` from `AI_CONTENT_BLOCKS` | 1005–1012 |
| 3 | New `ScreeningRequirementsPanel` component | new, near 633 |
| 4 | Swap the textarea for the panel | 6459–6470 |
| 5 | Move Education/Experience selects out of `info` into the panel | 6344–6389 |
| 6 | Auto-apply the position's template in `applyPositionToDraft` | 4623 |
| 7 | Confirm-before-overwrite dialog | new state + dialog |
| 8 | Load vocabulary **eagerly** instead of only on card flip | 3103 |
| 9 | Publish gate → "≥1 *recognised* skill" | 3553 |
| 10 | Reword the Entities-Indicated hints | 842, 885 |

**Backend, NLP service, database: zero changes.** `draft.skills` stays a newline-delimited string, still saved to `skills_json`, still read by `ScreeningService::buildRequirements`, still rendered on the public careers page.

## What each part gives you

**Point 1 — "remove Required Skills":** the free-text textarea is gone. HR never types a duty, a degree or a sentence into a skills box, because the only way to add a skill is to pick a recognised term from the vocabulary.

**Point 2 — "where do I replace the input":** into this panel, which auto-populates from the position's requirement template. If a position has no template, the panel shows "No requirement template for this position — [Create one]" and offers a `+ Add skill` combobox as the fallback.

**Point 3 — "auto-connect entities to the job position":** `applyPositionToDraft` already syncs salary from the position's grade. This extends it one step: pick a position → find its active template via `position_id` → auto-apply if the draft is empty, or ask first if you've already typed something. Combined with the panel, choosing a position is now the *only* action needed to get a screenable post.

# Plan: Replace the Required Skills textarea with a position-driven Screening Requirements panel

## Locked decisions
1. **UI** → structured requirements block (chips + vocabulary feedback + autocomplete)
2. **Auto-apply** → ask before replacing hand-typed skills
3. **AI** → skills removed from AI fill entirely
4. **Education/Experience** → move out of `info` into the panel
5. **No-template fallback** → offer inline template creation

## Why this is safe`skills_json` stays exactly as it is. `'skills' => ['nullable','array']` in both `StoreJobPostRequest:40` and `UpdateJobPostRequest:40`, so nothing on the backend blocks us. `draft.skills` remains a newline-delimited string, still written by the payload builder at line 3279, still read by `ScreeningService::buildRequirements` (`ScreeningService.php:48`), still rendered on the careers page (`jobs.index.tsx:247`). **No backend, no migration, no NLP change.**

## The change set — 11 edits, all in `RecruitmentManagement.tsx`

| # | Edit | Lines |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Relabel block `Required Skills` → `Screening Requirements` | 996 |
| 2 | Remove `"skills"` from `AI_CONTENT_BLOCKS` | 1005–1012 |
| 3 | New `ScreeningRequirementsPanel` component | new, after 706 |
| 4 | Swap the textarea for the panel | 6459–6470 |
| 5 | Move Education + Experience selects into the panel | 6344–6389 |
| 6 | Auto-apply the position's template in `applyPositionToDraft` | 4623–4667 |
| 7 | Confirm-before-overwrite dialog (`pendingTemplate` state) | new |
| 8 | Load screening vocabulary eagerly instead of on card flip | 3070, 3083, 3103 |
| 9 | Publish gate → "≥1 **recognised** skill" | 3553–3566 |
| 10 | Add optional pre-seed prop to `RequirementTemplateManager` | 1298 |
| 11 | Reword Entities-Indicated hints | 842, 853, 885 |

### Notes per edit

**3 / 4 — The panel.** Reuses the helpers already in the file, so recognition answers match the screener exactly:
- `buildBuilderEntityIndex` (506) to flatten the vocabulary
- `analyzeBuilderEntityLines` (549) to split `draft.skills` into recognized / unrecognized
- `BuilderEntityGroup` (634) for the chip rows — extended with an optional `onRemove` for the `✕`

**6 — Auto-apply.** Inside `applyPositionToDraft`, after the existing salary sync: resolve `position.dbId` → `requirementTemplates.find(t => t.active && t.position_id === dbId)` → if found and `draft.skills` is blank, apply silently; if skills already exist, set `pendingTemplate` and open the confirm dialog (mirroring the existing `confirmGenerateOpen` pattern at 3431). A `draftRef` gives read access to current draft state without re-creating the callback.

**8 — Eager vocabulary.** `loadEntityMapping` currently runs only when the card is flipped. The panel shows live ✓/◌ marks, so it must load when the builder tab opens.

**9 — Publish gate.** `AI_CONTENT_BLOCKS` no longer contains `skills`, so the old "block is non-empty" check falls away. Replace with: if `analyzeBuilderEntityLines(...).recognized.length === 0`, block publish with *"Add at least one skill the screener recognises"* — a genuinely stronger rule than today.

**10 — Inline creation.** `RequirementTemplateManager` owns its editor dialog internally (`editorOpen` at 1325). Add one optional prop, e.g. `autoCreateFor?: { positionId: string; positionTitle: string }`, that seeds `form.positionId` and opens the editor on mount. The panel's empty state renders it in a `Dialog`.

## Deliberately not changed

- The `Skills` group in `BuilderEntitiesCard` (839–854) keeps working unchanged — it reads the same `draft.skills`
- `applyRequirementTemplateToDraft` (2490) keeps its existing routing: skills → `draft.skills`, certs/roles/levels → `draft.qualifications` + the structured levels. It now just also auto-fires
- The Screening Setup dialog and its Scoring/Reference Data tabs

## Risks to watch

- **Positions sharing a title across departments** — `builderTemplateOptions` (3021) already matches on `dbId`, but `applyPositionToDraft` resolves the position via department + title. The auto-apply must use the same resolved object, not a title-only lookup.
- **Template with `position_id = null`** ("any position") — must not be auto-applied on every position change, or picking a job title would silently overwrite skills. Restrict auto-apply to exact `position_id` matches.
- **Existing published posts** — `jobToDraft` (1138) round-trips `j.skills.join("\n")` unchanged, so every live post opens in the panel with its skills already as chips. No data migration needed.

## Verification

1. New post → pick "Front Desk Officer" → skills chips appear automatically, template name shown
2. Publish is blocked until ≥1 skill shows ✓
3. `job_posts.skills_json` is non-empty and the careers page still lists the skills
4. Run screening on a test applicant → Skills criterion scores ~40 pts, coverage gate behaves
5. Pick a position with hand-typed skills → confirm dialog appears, cancel leaves skills intact
6. Position with no template → "Create requirements for this position" opens a pre-filled template editor; after saving, chips populate

<skill_content name="browser-automation">
# Skill: browser-automation

# browser-automation

Closes the edit → run → **look at it** → fix loop that otherwise requires the
user to describe what is on their screen.

## Usage

```bash
node <this-skill-dir>/browser.mjs <url> [options]
```

`<this-skill-dir>` is the folder you just read this file from — `browser.mjs`
sits beside it. Use that path literally rather than guessing at a home
directory.

| option | meaning |
|---|---|
| `--snapshot`        | list every interactive element with a clickable ref (add `--full` for the whole accessibility tree) |
| `--wait <selector>` | block until the selector appears (default: DOM ready) |
| `--eval <js>`       | run an expression in the page, print the JSON result |
| `--script <file>`   | drive a sequence — see **Scripting** below |
| `--screenshot <p>`  | write a PNG — read it afterwards to look at it |
| `--timeout <ms>`    | navigation timeout, default 30000 |
| `--session <id>`    | keep ONE page alive across calls — see **Sessions** below |
| `--close`           | with `--session <id>`, tear that session's browser down |

## Driving by ref, not by selector

`--snapshot` returns the page's interactive elements, each with a ref:

```
@e5 button "Audit my code"
@e9 button "Select your model" [haspopup=menu]
@e10 button "Manual" [haspopup=menu]
@e11 button "Send" [disabled]
```

Click `@e10` and you get what the page says is there — no selector to author
from a DOM you cannot see. This matters most for **icon-only buttons**, which
have no accessible name at all: `getByRole('button', {name: …})` cannot find
them, and they show up here as `@e1 button [haspopup=dialog]`.

A ref is stamped into the page, so it dies on navigation or a re-render.
**Re-snapshot after anything that changes the page** — the refs renumber, and a
stale one matches nothing.

`--full` returns the accessibility tree instead (headings, text, links). Use
refs to *act*, `--full` to *read*.

## Scripting a sequence

`--script` runs a file that default-exports `async (page, ui) => result`.

**`page` is a Playwright `Page`** (the driver is patchright, a Playwright fork),
so use the Playwright API — `page.locator`, `page.getByRole`, `page.getByText`,
`page.waitForFunction`, `page.evaluate`. It is NOT Puppeteer: `page.$` and
friends mostly work, but `getByRole` and `locator` do not exist there, so code
written against Puppeteer will fail in confusing ways.

**`ui` is the ref helper**, and is usually the shorter path:

| call | does |
|---|---|
| `await ui.snapshot()` | the ref listing above, as a string |
| `await ui.snapshot({full: true})` | the accessibility tree instead |
| `await ui.click('@e7')` | click that element |
| `await ui.fill('@e3', 'text')` | fill an input |
| `await ui.text('@e5')` | its inner text |
| `ui.ref('@e5')` | the raw locator, for anything else |

Whatever you return is printed as JSON. The runner owns the browser, the
console/network capture and the teardown; the script only drives and asserts.

```js
// qa.mjs  —  node <this-skill-dir>/browser.mjs http://localhost:3000 --script ./qa.mjs
export default async function run(page, ui) {
  // Look at what is there before deciding what to click.
  const before = await ui.snapshot()
  const signIn = before.match(/@(e\d+) button "Sign in"/)?.[1]
  if (!signIn) return { error: 'no sign-in button', snapshot: before }

  await ui.click(signIn)
  await page.waitForTimeout(500)

  // The page changed, so the old refs are gone — snapshot again.
  const after = await ui.snapshot()
  return { opened: after.includes('textbox'), after }
}
```

Navigation to the URL argument has already happened before your function runs.
You can navigate further with `page.goto(...)`.

## Read the text before the pixels

`--screenshot` writes a PNG and **you can read it** — a read of an image returns
the picture. If it comes back as `[binary file: png …]` this host has no image
path; say so rather than guessing at what rendered.

Even so, reach for text first. It is not just cheaper — it is more precise:

- `--snapshot` — every interactive element, with refs
- `--snapshot --full` — the accessibility tree: headings, text, links
- `--eval "…"` — ask the DOM a direct question
- the console/network report, which catches most breakage for almost nothing

A screenshot costs tens of thousands of tokens and answers "does this look
right", which is a narrower question than it seems. Use it for layout and visual
regressions, and use the tree for everything about structure, content and state.

## Interpreting the report

- `console.error` / uncaught exceptions → almost always a real bug.
- `requests failed` → a 404 on a JS chunk usually means a stale build is being
  served; a 500 means the server, not the page.
- `title` empty and `bodyChars` near zero → the app did not mount at all. Check
  the console section first, not the DOM.

## Examples

```bash
# Did my change render?
node <this-skill-dir>/browser.mjs http://localhost:3000

# Assert something specific about the DOM
node <this-skill-dir>/browser.mjs http://localhost:3000 \
  --eval "document.querySelectorAll('[data-testid=row]').length"

# Wait for a late-mounting element before judging the page
node <this-skill-dir>/browser.mjs http://localhost:3000 --wait "[data-testid=grid]"
```

## Gotchas found by using this

- **Keep the trailing slash** on a path-prefixed app. `http://host/app` and
  `http://host/app/` resolve relative asset URLs differently, and without it a
  page can return HTTP 200 with `bodyChars 0` and never mount. An app that 200s
  but renders nothing is usually this, not a crash.
- **A failing request is not automatically a bug.** Apps routinely probe for
  optional local services that are simply not running. Check whether the
  dependency is meant to exist before reporting it.
- **Never assert on text your own input put on the page.** A check for
  "console error" matches the prompt you just typed into the app as readily as
  the thing you were looking for, and the test passes while proving nothing.
  Match only strings that can come from the system under test.
- **Wait for content, not for a fixed delay.** A client-rendered app that is
  merely slow is indistinguishable from one that is broken unless you actually
  wait for something to appear.
- **Prefer a ref over a selector.** A selector that silently matches nothing and
  an element that is genuinely absent produce the same failure, and you cannot
  tell them apart without looking. `--snapshot` first, then act on what it
  listed. When a check still says something is missing, use `--snapshot --full`
  to read the tree before reporting it, and screenshot if the question is
  genuinely visual.
- Third-party analytics failures are filtered out; they are noise, not signal.

## One run, one browser (the default)

By default each invocation launches a browser, does the work, and closes it.
Cookies, logins and page state do **not** survive to the next invocation, so a
short sequence should happen inside a single `--script` run rather than across
several calls. This is the right default: most QA is "load this, tell me what
broke."

## Sessions — keep one page alive across calls

When you need to *think between steps* — drive a form, read the result, decide
the next action, drive again — a single `--script` can't help, because you don't
know step 3 until you've seen step 2. Use `--session <id>`: the browser stays
alive between separate invocations and every call reconnects to the **same page**
it left open.

```bash
# Step 1: open the app in a named session, set something up
node <this-skill-dir>/browser.mjs http://localhost:3000 --session qa1 --snapshot

# Step 2: NO url — act on the page the session already has open
node <this-skill-dir>/browser.mjs --session qa1 --eval "document.querySelector('#total').innerText"

# Step 3: re-navigate within the same session if you want, or keep acting
node <this-skill-dir>/browser.mjs --session qa1 --script ./next-step.mjs

# When done — always tear it down, or the browser stays running
node <this-skill-dir>/browser.mjs --session qa1 --close
```

Rules:
- **Omit the url** on follow-up calls to act on the current page; **pass a url**
  to navigate the session's page somewhere new.
- Refs from `--snapshot` still die on navigation/re-render — re-snapshot after
  anything that changes the page, same as one-shot mode.
- **Always `--close` when finished.** The browser is detached and outlives the
  call by design; without `--close` it keeps running until the machine reboots.
- Sessions are headless and use a throwaway profile per id under
  `~/.codegpt/ab-sessions/` — never the user's real browser or cookies.

## Notes

- Resolves `patchright` from an installed CodeGPT extension, then a dev
  checkout, then a global copy — so it normally needs no install of its own. If
  none is found it says what it looked for.
- Headless. It never touches the user's real browser profile or cookies.

**Bug A (step 10) — the no-template empty state doesn't show.**
When selecting `hr` (no template), `onPositionChange` does `if(!tpl){ render(); return; }`. But `render()` reads `STATE.tpl` which is still the OLD template (Front Office Officer). So the banner shows the stale template instead of the empty state. `srcTag` correctly says "No template for this position" but the banner and chips are stale.

Real fix: when there's no template for the new position, we must not pretend the previous template is still the source. Options:
- Show the empty-state banner (regardless of STATE.tpl) when the current position has no template.

The mockup is ready and verified.

**`TRASH/preview-screening-requirements-panel.html`** — open it in your browser. There's a **BEFORE / AFTER** toggle at the top.

## What it does

**AFTER tab** is fully interactive — switch positions, add skills, remove them, publish.

- **Pick a position** → its requirement template resolves and the skills/certs appear as chips automatically
- **Chips** show live `✓` recognised / `◌` to-review, using the same vocabulary the screener matches against
- **`+`** on a grey chip adds that term to the reference data
- **`+ Add skill`** is a combobox over the vocabulary — so you can't type a skill that won't match
- **Education / Experience** now live in the panel (moved out of Job Info), since those are screening entities worth 20 + 30 points
- **Publish gate** blocks unless at least one skill is *recognised* — much stronger than today's "box isn't empty"
- **Confirm dialog** appears when you switch position on a post that already has requirements, and shows exactly what will be added and removed
- A position with **no template** shows an empty state with "Create requirements for this position", and **keeps** whatever skills were already on the post instead of silently wiping them

**BEFORE tab** shows the current textarea next to the exact consequences of deleting it (`required_skills → []`, skills criterion 0/40, coverage gate dead, post drops out of open-job recommendations, public careers page loses its skills list).

## Verification

I drove all 12 flows in a real browser — 0 console errors. Two genuine bugs surfaced and are fixed:

1. **Stale provenance** — selecting a position with no template still showed the *previous* template's banner, so the "create requirements" empty state never appeared. Now provenance is tracked separately from the dropdown, so it reports honestly.
2. **Wrong math** — the coverage line hardcoded "must match at least 3 of these 5" regardless of actual count. Now computed from the real total, and it names the specific unrecognised terms.

I also hit a combobox bug worth flagging for the real implementation: an outside-click listener closed the dropdown on the same click that opened it, because the opener button sits outside the dropdown container. The mockup now excludes openers explicitly — **the real panel will need the same guard.**
