Let me be concrete and useful. The core problem: users end up putting skills content into Responsibilities/Qualifications because the Required Skills textarea is a blank slate.

Alternatives worth considering:

**Alternative 1: Don't add a new panel — make Responsibilities/Qualifications themselves entity-aware.**
Keep exactly the blocks they have, but run every line through the entity analyzer live. As HR types into Responsibilities, lines that match the skills vocabulary get tagged "this is a skill" with a one-click "move to Required Skills" action. So skills get *extracted* from where they naturally land rather than being asked for in a separate box.
- Pro: zero new UI, no new block, HR never thinks about skills.
- Con: still 3 text blocks; extraction is heuristic.

**Alternative 2: Merge skills into Qualifications, drop the separate block entirely.**
One "Qualifications & Requirements" block. Lines are auto-classified into skill vs cert vs education by the existing regex + vocabulary. `skills_json` is derived at save time from the classified lines.
- Pro: reduces 3 boxes → 2, which is the real complaint.
- Con: needs a classifier at save time; risks polluting required_skills with sentences. Needs a new save-time derivation step.

**Alternative 3: Position-first wizard instead of a drag-and-drop canvas.**
Rather than a block on the canvas, make the builder a short guided flow: 1) pick position 2) requirements auto-load (read-only, from template) 3) write the prose (AI-assisted) 4) publish. Requirements are not a block at all — they're a read-only summary of the template, because they should be standardized per role anyway.
- Pro: strongest guarantee of consistency, very fast, no duplication possible.
- Con: removes the drag-drop customization entirely; big change; HR can't tweak per posting.

**Alternative 4: Keep the block but change the input type only — a tag/chip picker with no other redesign.**
Just replace the textarea with a multi-select combobox writing to `draft.skills`. No auto-apply, no education/experience move, no gate change.
- Pro: smallest diff, ~1 edit, solves "I can't tell what's recognized".
- Con: doesn't address the duplication or the auto-fill ask.

**Alternative 5: Make the vocabulary do the work — auto-suggest skills from the title.**
When a position is picked, suggest skills from the vocabulary ranked by relevance to the title/department, as one-click chips. No template needed at all.
- Pro: works even with zero templates configured; simplest mental model.

## The alternatives| # | Approach | How it works | Trade-off |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1** | **Live entity tagging in the blocks you already have** | Keep all3 textareas. Every line you type is run through the vocabulary *as you type*. A Responsibilities line that is really a skill gets tagged `this is a skill` with a one-click **Move to Requirements**. | Skills get *extracted* from where they naturally land instead of being asked for separately. Zero new UI. But still 3 boxes. |
| **2** | **Merge skills into Qualifications** | One block: "Qualifications & Requirements". Each line is auto-classified as skill / cert / education at save time, and `skills_json` is *derived* from the classified lines. | Genuinely removes a box (3 → 2). But classification is a heuristic — a badly written sentence can still leak into `required_skills` and pollute scoring. |
| **3** | **Position-first wizard, requirements not a block at all** | Replace the drag-and-drop canvas with: ① pick position ② requirements load from the template **read-only** ③ write the prose (AI-assisted) ④ publish. Requirements become a summary panel, not an editable block. | Strongest consistency guarantee — per-role requirements can't drift between postings. Fastest to complete. But removes drag-drop customisation entirely. |
| **4** | **Chip picker only** | Just swap the textarea for a vocabulary combobox writing to `draft.skills`. Nothing else changes. | Smallest diff (~1 edit), fixes "I can't tell what's recognised". Doesn't touch the duplication or add any auto-fill. |
| **5** | **Suggest skills from the position title** | On position pick, rank vocabulary terms by relevance to the title/department and offer them as one-click suggestions. Uses the template when one exists, keyword match when not. | Works even with **zero** templates configured — the weakest point of the design I proposed. |

## Where I'd push back on my own proposal

The panel I built has a soft spot: **it depends on a requirement template existing.** If HR never configures one, the panel is just a fancier empty textbox, and you land back in the same place. Alternatives 5 and 3 both have a fallback that doesn't depend on HR doing setup work first.

The strongest combination is probably **1 + 3**: keep the prose blocks you have, tag and extract entities inline as you type, and drive requirements from the position. That removes the "three boxes competing" problem *and* the "nothing loads unless someone set up a template" problem.

out.push({c:k, a:map[k]}); }); return out; }\nfunction norm(s){ return String(s).toLowerCase().trim().replace(/\\s+/g,\" \"); }\nfunction canonicalize(text, map){\n  var n=norm(text); if(!n) return if(norm(entries[i].a[j])===n) return entries[i].c;\n    }\n  }\n  /* boundary-substring, longest key first */\n  var keys=[];\n  entries.forEach(function(e){\n    keys.push([norm(e.c),e.c]);\n function canonicalize(text, map){
  var n=norm(text); if(!n) return null;
  var entries=flat(map);
  for(var i=0;i<entries.length;i++){
    if(norm(entries[i].c)===n) return entries[i].c;
    for(var j=0;j<entries[i].a.length;j++){
      if(norm(entries[i].a[j])===n) return entries[i].c;
    }
  }
  /* boundary-substring, longest key first */
  var keys=[];
  entries.forEach(function(e){
    keys.push([norm(e.c),e.c]);
    e.a.forEach(function(a){ keys.push([norm(a),e.c]); });
  });
  keys.sort(function(a,b){ return b[0].length-a[0].length; });
  var padded=" "+n+" ";
  for(var k=0;k<keys.length;k++){
    if(keys[k][0].length>=4 && padded.indexOf(" "+keys[k][0]+" ")>=-1) return keys[k][1];
  }
  return null;
}

## Assistant

**`TRASH/preview-wizard-live-tagging.html`** — Alternative B, fully interactive. Walk steps 1→4.

## How it differs from the first mockup

**Step 1 — Position.** Choose the role; salary band, vacancies and the requirement template are all read from Core HCM. Nothing hand-typed.

**Step 2 — Requirements.** Derived, not a box to fill. From the template when one exists. When it doesn't — the soft spot I flagged in the first design — you get **ranked suggestions from the role title** instead of a blank, plus "create a template". So it works on day one with zero setup.

**Step 3 — Write.** This is the "1" in1+3. Every line you type is analysed immediately. `Knife Skills` buried in Responsibilities gets flagged **recognised skill → Knife Skills** with *Move to requirements* / *Move & delete the line*. Lines already counted show greyed under *"already in the requirements — not counted twice"*, so nothing gets double-scored. Requirement-shaped lines that aren't in the vocabulary get flagged but explicitly left alone: *"keep as prose"*.

**Step 4 — Review.** The gate, plus a plain statement of where requirements came from.

Your original complaint — skills ending up in Responsibilities and Qualifications — is now caught **at the moment it happens**, instead of discovered later on a card most people never flip.

## Three real bugs found while testing

Worth flagging because two would have hit the actual implementation:

1. **`<textarea>` has a `.type` IDL property.** An inline handler compiled with `with(this)` resolved my `type(...)` function to the string `"textarea"` and threw `TypeError` — silently, inside an event handler. Renamed to `onFieldInput`. If anyone ever writes a React handler named `type` wired to a textarea, same trap.
2. **`indexOf(...) >= -1`** in the canonicalizer — always true, since `indexOf` returns `-1` on a miss. Every line "matched" the longest key in the vocabulary. Your production code uses `.includes()`, which is boolean, so **`RecruitmentManagement.tsx` is unaffected** — this was only in my mockup.
3. Responsibilities and Qualifications had **no `oninput` at all** — live tagging silently dead in the two boxes that matter most.

Verified: 12 flows driven in a real browser, 0 console errors.

## Trade-off to be aware of

This replaces the drag-and-drop canvas with a linear wizard. You get consistency and speed, but **HR loses per-post block reordering and customisation**. If that's not acceptable, the honest fallback is keeping the canvas and layering the live tagging onto the existing Responsibilities/Qualifications blocks only — no wizard. Say the word and I'll mock that variant too, or go ahead and implement whichever you prefer.

## The one part that really matters

Screening vocabulary (terms the applicant-screening model recognizes):
- SKILLS: Front Office Operations; Guest Relations; Reservations; …
- CERTIFICATIONS: TESDA NC II Cookery; Food Handler Certificate; …

```

So the AI is deliberately constrained to emit terms the screener can actually match. That's the whole reason generated posts used to produce meaningful `fit_score` numbers.

## What this means for your three designs

| Design | What happens to the AI's skills output |
|---|---|
| **A — Requirements panel** | AI no longer fills skills at all. They come from the position's template. The prompt's rule 4 and the `skills_matched`/`skills_new` report become dead code and should be removed. |
| **B — Wizard + live tagging** | Same as A, but you could still ask the AI for *suggestions* to seed step 2. |
| **C — Derived from prose** | AI's `skills[]` must be **appended as lines into Qualifications**, then re-derived. The `skills_new` report maps perfectly onto the "produced no entity" lines. |

## Why C actually fits the AI better than A

Under C the AI's grounding report stops being a side note and becomes the UI. The mockup already shows it: lines that match get `✓ recognised skill → Complaint Handling`, lines that don't get `no vocabulary entity — kept as prose, contributes 0 points`. That **is** `skills_new`, rendered where HR can act on it with one click.

Under A, the AI's skill generation is thrown away entirely and the vocabulary grounding for skills becomes pointless.

## Two things I'd flag before you decide

1. **The prompt caps skills at 150 and certs at 60.** As your vocabulary grows past that, the AI silently stops seeing terms. Worth checking your current `screening_reference_data` count against those caps.
2. **Under C, AI-generated *responsibilities* prose becomes load-bearing.** Today a badly-worded duty line just reads oddly on the ad. Under C, a duty line the vocabulary can't parse contributes 0 points to screening. The prompt's rules for `responsibilities` (line 807) say nothing about vocabulary — that would need to change if you go with C.

## What AI does today

You click **"Generate with AI"**. It writes the boring parts of the job post for you — the description, the duties, the requirements, and a list of skills.

**The important bit:** before writing, the system shows the AI your screening vocabulary — the list of terms your resume screener recognises (like `Front Office Operations`, `TESDA NC II Cookery`). Then it tells the AI: *"use these exact words for the skills."*

Why? Because if the AI invents its own words like "Guest Interaction Proficiency", your screener won't recognise it, and the applicant will score 0 for having that skill.

Afterwards it tells you: *"3 of those skills you can already match, 1 is new — add it to your vocabulary."*

**There's no AI button in it.** On purpose.

I removed AI from skills. Because in that design, skills come from the **requirement template** — the one your HR team writes once per job role. No AI needed; it's just a lookup.

## In the design you picked last (derived)

This one is actually **better** for AI.

Instead of the AI handing you a skills list, it writes normal sentences. Then the system reads those sentences and pulls the skills back out.

So it becomes:

```
AI writes:  "Handle guest inquiries and complaints professionally."
System reads:  → that's "Complaint Handling"  ✓ counts
```

The new-words warning still works — but now it's **shown live, right under the box**, instead of buried in a toast message. You see immediately which lines worked and which didn't.

Under this design, the AI's job gets slightly harder. A duty line it writes badly won't match anything, and will score 0.

So I'd need to also tell the AI: *"write the duties using words from this vocabulary too"* — not just the skills. Small change to one instruction.

## What it sendsOnly the ticked fields and their notes — plus your screening vocabulary, which the backend adds automatically so the AI reuses terms your screener already recognises.

## The report tells you the truth

```
Skills         1 added to Screening Requirements
               ● Service Upselling — new, press + to add to the vocabulary
Certificates   0 added
Education      Bachelor's Degree
Experience     1-2 Years
Skipped        (nothing ticked here)
```

The "new term" warning is the important part — same idea as the real backend's `skills_new` report. That term won't match any resume until you press `+`.

Unticked fields are listed as **Skipped** and are genuinely left alone — untick Skills and no skills are written, even though the vocabulary still goes to the AI.

## Verified

Driven in a real browser: all 6 checkboxes + 6 note boxes present, untick-all disables Generate, notes steer both skills and education, unticked fields skipped, and generated skills land as chips in the Screening Requirements panel. 0 console errors.

Two bugs caught and fixed while testing: the notes regex was matching the *negation* ("skip anything technical" read as a request **for** technical skills), and re-running the AI was appending duplicate skills every click instead of deduping.

Done. **Generate with AI** is now a button in the builder header that opens a modal.

## How it works

Click **Generate with AI** → modal opens with the checklist. Nothing is rendered on the page until you click it.

Inside the modal:
- **6 rows** — Position · Department · Skills · Certificate · Education · Experience
- Each has a **checkbox** (tick what you want) and its **own notes box** (your guidance for the AI)
- Untick everything → **Generate** goes disabled and rows grey out
- **Generate** runs it, and the result report appears inside the modal
- **Close** / **Escape** / clicking the backdrop all dismiss it

The results are already applied to your draft before the modal closes — so the new chips are sitting in the Screening Requirements panel when you get back.

## The report```
Skills         1 added to Screening Requirements
               ● Service Upselling — new, press + to add to the vocabulary
Certificates   0 added
Education      Bachelor's Degree
Experience     3-5 Years
Skipped        (nothing ticked)
```

# Plan: transform the mockup into your real Job Post Builder

## The design, in one picture

```
Job Title
Job Info Type · Schedule · Vacancies · Salary
Screening Requirements ◄── Position dropdown  [THE CONTROL]
                              From template "…Requirements" · 5 skills, 1 cert
                              Skills        ✓ chips + combobox + ✕ remove
                              Certifications ✓ chips
                              Education level ▾
                              Experience level  ▾
Job Description
Key Responsibilities
Qualifications
Additional Info ← NEW block
Application Instruction
About Company
Picture of Hiring
```

Plus: **Generate with AI** button → modal with *Always sent* (6 read-only values) and *Choose what to generate* (6 checkboxes, each with its own notes box).

---

## The gap between mockup and reality

| Mockup | Reality |
|---|---|
| Chips with ✓/✕/combobox | `draft.skills` is a plain newline string |
| Education/Experience in the panel | Selects live in `info` (6344–6389) |
| Position inside the panel | Select lives in `title` block (6186) |
| AI checklist + notes | One button, no checklist, no notes |
| Additional Info block | **Does not exist** |
| Instructions / About filled | **Never saved** — dropped at3579–3602 |
| Publish gate on recognised skills | Gate on "block is non-empty" (3553) |

The last two are the real work. Everything else is reshaping.

---

## Part 1 — Frontend (13 edits, `RecruitmentManagement.tsx`)

**Block registry**
1. `996` — relabel `Required Skills` → `Screening Requirements`
2. `1002, 979-988` — insert `"additional"` into `BlockId` and `fullBlocks`, after `qualifications`
3. `1005-1012` — drop `"skills"` from `AI_CONTENT_BLOCKS`

**Draft state**
4. `1087-1110` — add `additional: string`
5. `1112-1131` — `blankDraft.additional = ""`
6. `1138-1162` — `jobToDraft`: `additional: j.additional.join("\n")`

**Block JSX**
7. `6459-6470` — swap the textarea for `<ScreeningRequirementsPanel>`
8. `6344-6389` — move the education/experience selects into the panel
9. `6214-6416` — `info` block shrinks from ~200 to ~90 lines
10. new — the `additional` block after `qualifications` (6507)

**New component**
11. after `706` — `ScreeningRequirementsPanel`, reusing `buildBuilderEntityIndex` (506), `canonicalizeBuilderEntity` (520), `analyzeBuilderEntityLines` (549), `BuilderEntityGroup` (634). Writes to the same `draft.skills` string, so `JobPostResource`, `ScreeningService` and the careers page are untouched.

**Behaviour**
12. `4623` — `applyPositionToDraft` auto-applies the position's template
13. `3553` — publish gate becomes "≥1 **recognised** skill"

---

## Part 2 — Backend (5 new touchpoints)

This did not exist before. Additional Info needs a column, and Instructions/About are currently discarded.

| # | File | Change |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | new migration | `additional_json`, `instructions_json`, `about_json` (all `json nullable`) |
| 2 | `JobPost.php` | add to `$fillable` + `casts` as `array` |
| 3 | `Store/UpdateJobPostRequest` | `'additional' => ['nullable','array']`, same for `instructions`/`about` |
| 4 | `RecruitmentManagementController` `store()`201-207 / `update()` 320-322 | map to the `_json` columns |
| 5 | `JobPostResource` `:47` | expose `additional`, `instructions`, `about` |

Then frontend `Job` type (`api.ts`), payload build (`3579`, `3715`), `jobToDraft`, and the public careers page (`jobs.$jobId.tsx`).

> **Decision needed:** persisting Instructions and About fixes a pre-existing bug, but it changes the careers page layout. Do you want that, or should I persist only `additional` and leave the other two as they are today?

---

## Part 3 — The AI change

14. `3424` — `generateDraftWithAI` opens the modal instead of running directly
15. `3438-3457` — payload becomes `{ ticked_blocks, notes, context }`; **also add `experience_level` + `education_level`, which are accepted by the backend (`:442-443`) but never sent today**
16. `JobContentGenerator::buildPrompt` `779-816` — rework from "return 6 keys" to "return only the ticked blocks, honouring each note"
17. `889-897` — `BuilderEntitiesCard` reads skills from the panel, not `draft.skills`
18. `2490-2566` — `applyRequirementTemplateToDraft` routes to the panel

---

## Risks

| Risk | Why it bites |
|---|---|
| **Deleting the skills field wipes existing posts** | `jobToDraft:1154` is the only read path. Existing `skills_json` must be folded back into the draft or the next save destroys them. **This is the highest-risk edit.** |
| Vocabulary must load eagerly | `loadEntityMapping` (3083) currently runs only on card flip (3103). The panel shows live ✓ marks, so it must load on mount. |
| Shared job titles across departments | `applyPositionToDraft` resolves position by department + title. Auto-apply must use that same resolved object, not a title-only lookup. |
| `position_id = null` templates | Must **not** auto-apply, or picking any job title would overwrite requirements. |

## Order of work

1. Backend columns + resource (nothing else can persist)
2. `jobToDraft` safety net **first** — before any UI change
3. Panel + block swap (frontend only, reversible)
4. Position auto-apply + confirm dialog
5. Publish gate
6. AI modal

Steps 1–2 alone fix real data loss; 3–6 are the redesign.

503: interface BuilderEntityIndex {
504:   exact: Map<string, string>;

508: /** Flattens {canonical: aliases} into an exact lookup plus longest-first keys. */
509: function buildBuilderEntityIndex(mapping: Record<string, string[]>): BuilderEntityIndex {
510:   const exact = new Map<string, string>();
511:   Object.entries(mapping ?? {}).forEach(([canonical, aliases]) => {
512:     const canonKey = normalizeEntityText(canonical);
513:     if (canonKey && !exact.has(canonKey)) exact.set(canonKey, canonical);
514:     (aliases ?? []).forEach((alias) => {
515:       const key = normalizeEntityText(alias);
516:       if (key && !exact.has(key)) exact.set(key, canonical);
517:     });
518:   });
519:   return { exact, keys: [...exact.keys()].sort((a, b) => b.length - a.length) };
520: }
521: 
522: /** Exact → boundary-substring → token-containment, like the NLP service. */
523: function canonicalizeBuilderEntity(value: string, index: BuilderEntityIndex): string | null {
524:   const norm = normalizeEntityText(value);
525:   if (!norm) return null;
526:   const direct = index.exact.get(norm);
527:   if (direct) return direct;
528:   const padded = ` ${norm} `;
529:   for (const key of index.keys) {
530:     if (key.length >= 4 && padded.includes(` ${key} `)) return index.exact.get(key) ?? null;
531:   }
532:   const valueTokens = new Set(norm.split(" "));
533:   let best: string | null = null;
534:   let bestLen = 0;
535:   for (const key of index.keys) {
536:     const keyTokens = key.split(" ");
537:     if (keyTokens.length < 2 || key.length <= bestLen) continue;
538:     if (keyTokens.every((t) => valueTokens.has(t))) {
539:       best = index.exact.get(key) ?? null;
540:       bestLen = key.length;
541:     }
542:   }
543:   return best;
544: }

608: function builderScoringFromConfig(

614:       name.toLowerCase().includes(match),

622:   const passingRaw = Number((effective as { passing_score?: unknown }).passing_score);

627:       education: findWeight("education", 20),

630:     passingScore: Number.isFinite(passingRaw) ? passingRaw : 75,
631:     coverageMin: Number.isFinite(coverageRaw) ? coverageRaw : 0.6,

Done. The preview is now your real Job Post Builder. Here's what changed:

## Backend (all `php -l` clean, tests pass)
- **New migration** `2026_10_13_000001_add_additional_instructions_about_to_job_posts_table.php` — adds `additional_json` (JSON), `instructions` + `about` (text), all nullable. No columns or tables removed.
- `JobPost.php` — the three fields added to `$fillable` + `additional_json` cast to `array`.
- `StoreJobPostRequest` / `UpdateJobPostRequest` — `'additional' => ['nullable','array']`, `'instructions'/'about' => ['nullable','string']`.
- `RecruitmentManagementController` — `store()` maps `additional` → `additional_json`; `update()` mirrors it; `generateDraft()` accepts `blocks[]` + `notes{}`, passes them plus `experience_level`/`education_level` to the generator, and the grounding report now scans generated prose for vocabulary terms (skills are no longer generated).
- `JobContentGenerator::buildPrompt` — generates **only the ticked blocks**, honours each block's note, and no longer asks for a `skills` key. `normalize()` handles `additional`.
- Both `JobPostResource`s (Recruitment + Landing) expose the three new fields.

## Frontend
- **Screening Requirements panel** replaces the Required Skills textarea (`RecruitmentManagement.tsx`): Position picker on top (drives the template), template banner, Skills as vocabulary chips with ✓/+/✕ and a combobox, Certifications derived read-only from Qualifications, Education/Experience shown read-only (they stay editable in Job Info, per your call).
- **Additional Info** block below Qualifications, persisted end-to-end.
- **Instructions + About now persist** — they were silently dropped before; saved posts reload them instead of resetting to defaults.
- **Position auto-apply** with confirm-before-overwrite dialog (shows +will add / −will remove).
- **Publish gate** requires all six prose blocks *plus* ≥1 recognised skill (falls back to any skill line if the vocabulary hasn't loaded).
- **Generate with AI is now a modal**: read-only context (Position, Department, Skills, Certificate, Education, Experience) + the six checkboxes `Job Description, Key Responsibilities, Qualifications, Additional Info, Application Instruction, About Company`, each with its own notes box. Prose blocks replace, bullet blocks merge without duplicating; report shows reused vocabulary terms.
- Public job page renders Additional Info, How to Apply, and About Company sections.

## Verification
- `php -l` clean on all six backend files + migration.
- `tsc --noEmit`: only the pre-existing `FileCheck` error remains — nothing new.
- `JobContentGeneratorTest`: 9/9 pass. `ScreeningRequirementTemplateTest`: 2/2 pass.

## Two things to know
1. **Run the migration** (`php artisan migrate`) — until then, saving Additional Info/Instructions/About will fail validation at the DB layer.
2. I did **not** commit anything — the tree already had unrelated uncommitted work, and this repo syncs to Lovable. Say the word if you want a commit, and tell me whether to include only these files.

## Assistant

_Thinking:_



Removed the local remnants. Now the important part — what that does and doesn't do.

## Why I mentioned it

`frontend/AGENTS.md` contained a Lovable notice instructing any agent working in this repo not to rewrite pushed git history, because pushes to the connected branch sync back into the Lovable editor. That's the only reason I brought it up.

## What I just removed

- `frontend/AGENTS.md` — the file was *only* that notice (10 lines, nothing else), so I deleted the file.
- `frontend/src/lib/lovable-error-reporting.ts` — dead code, imported nowhere. Verified zero references before deleting.

I left alone: the `README.md` mentions (docs text only), the `bunfig.toml` package excludes (harmless), and the stale `bun.lock` entries (not the live lockfile — `package-lock.json` is, and it has no Lovable packages). Your `package.json` and `vite.config.ts` have zero Lovable dependencies, so the build never touched it.

## What this does NOT do

The actual sync is server-side: **Lovable dashboard ↔ your GitHub repo** (`Franzwll/2nd-repo-for-hrms-backend-`). Deleting local files cannot break that connection — pushing to the connected branch will still show up in the Lovable editor.

To fully disconnect, you have to do it where the connection lives (needs your login, I can't do it from here):

1. In Lovable: project → **Settings → GitHub → Disconnect** (or remove the project).
2. In GitHub: **Settings → Applications → Lovable → Revoke**, if you want it fully gone.

Once that's done, the history-rewrite caution no longer applies and you're free to rebase/squash normally.
